newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse lower despite second tier advance.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse lower despite second tier advance.

text.p: Second-tier issues performed well on the Bucharest stock market on Wednesday, with most average and closing prices advancing, but losses to first tier stocks pulled the market average down.
"Local and foreign investors paid increased attention to cheaper stocks in a bull run for smaller capitalisation companies extended from previous days," said a trader.
The average price of 23 of the 39 stocks on the lower tier climbed, seven fell and two remained unchanged. Six companies had no trade and one was suspended, a bourse report showed.
On the first tier, all but one of eight listings lost ground. "Buyers viewed prices in this category as high and they were reluctant to pay more," a broker said.
Sofert SOFE.BX fertiliser maker, whose average price was three percent up at 42,724 lei, closed at 42,500 lei, 1,400 up from Tuesday.

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, slipped by 0.6, 0.24 and 0.56 percent respectively from Tuesday due to falls in the average prices of top-tier stocks.
Traders said they expected the bullish phase to remain prominent in the second tier for the rest of the week. Some blue chips were expected to slip further.
The first tier took the bulk of the session's volume and turnover thanks to greater liquidity, operators said.
Total volume was 3.7 million shares, up from 3.3 million on Tuesday. Turnover rose by some 1.4 billion lei to 17.9 billion.

Adding to the session's turnover was some 1.8 billion lei from a special trade in high-cap Antibiotice ATBE.BX pharmaceutical. The deal involved more than 192,000 shares. Antibiotice closed 300 lei weaker at 8,800.
